Infrastructure, transparent rules and clear legal boundaries positioned as the core of the funded-account model

Octrado introduces its proprietary trading, a service that gives traders access to firm capital through a structured evaluation process. Under the model "Your Skill. Our Capital", the platform positions itself between the retail trader and the funded-account system, with the emphasis placed on the operational layer – data environment, rule clarity, evaluation and payouts – rather than on headline account sizes alone.

The programme follows a simple sequence: the trader registers, selects a programme, meets the stated conditions of the challenge, and — on passing — receives funded trader status with a share of the potentital profits generated. The design principle is that a trader must know in advance what is measured, what the limits are, when a rule is considered breached, and what the route from challenge to payout looks like.
Communicated programme parameters
The offering includes:
profit split of up to 90%
account sizes of up to USD 100,000
leverage of up to 1:100
the option to hold positions overnight, subject to programme rules
a restricted weekend trading regime
defined rules for trading around news releases

The offering also includes trading reports, tracking of trade success rate, drawdown and progress, educational materials, and client support. In an environment where selection is demanding, these elements determine whether a challenge is perceived as a fair test or as an opaque filter.

The professionalisation of proprietary trading is not a question of a better interface. It is the ability to maintain a consistent system — the same rules before and after the challenge, clear documentation, auditable reporting, and a legally correct separation of simulation from the live market. Where a platform holds those layers together, its position in the ecosystem rests on an infrastructure of trust rather than on the marketing of funded accounts.

Prop-trading surges in its volume. In its recent study, analysts of Octrado provided a global estimate, which puts the primary prop-trading market, the direct annual revenue of prop firms, at USD 4.0 to 4.5 billion, and the broader ecosystem value, which adds downstream brokerage fees and notionally allocated capital, at around USD 20 billion.
